cards.back: A flat or curved surface of a 3D shape.
cards.say: Face. A flat or curved surface of a 3D shape.

cards.back: A line where two faces meet.
cards.say: Edge. A line where two faces meet.

cards.back: A corner where edges meet.
cards.say: Vertex of a 3D shape. A corner where edges meet.

cards.back: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices. All faces are squares.
cards.say: Cube: faces, edges, vertices. Six faces, twelve edges, eight vertices. All faces are squares.

figure.alt: A cube with six square faces.

cards.back: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices. Faces are rectangles.
cards.say: Cuboid: faces, edges, vertices. Six faces, twelve edges, eight vertices. Faces are rectangles.

cards.back: 5 faces, 8 edges, 5 vertices. One square face and 4 triangle faces.
cards.say: Square-based pyramid: faces, edges, vertices. Five faces, eight edges, five vertices. One square face and four triangle faces.

cards.back: 5 faces, 9 edges, 6 vertices. 2 triangle faces and 3 rectangle faces.
cards.say: Triangular prism: faces, edges, vertices. Five faces, nine edges, six vertices. Two triangle faces and three rectangle faces.

cards.back: 1 curved face. No edges and no vertices.
cards.say: Sphere: faces and vertices. One curved face. No edges and no vertices.

cards.back: 2 flat circle faces and 1 curved face.
cards.say: Cylinder: faces. Two flat circle faces and one curved face.

figure.alt: A cylinder like a tin can.

cards.back: 1 flat circle face, 1 curved face and 1 vertex (the point).
cards.say: Cone: faces and vertices. One flat circle face, one curved face and one vertex, the point.

cards.front: How many faces does a cube have?
cards.say: How many faces does a cube have? Six.

cards.front: How many edges does a cube have?
cards.say: How many edges does a cube have? Twelve.

cards.front: How many vertices does a cuboid have?
cards.say: How many vertices does a cuboid have? Eight.

cards.front: How many triangle faces does a square-based pyramid have?
cards.say: How many triangle faces does a square-based pyramid have? Four.

cards.front: What shape are the faces of a cube?
cards.back: Squares.
cards.say: What shape are the faces of a cube? Squares.

cards.front: What shape are the 2 ends of a triangular prism?
cards.back: Triangles.
cards.say: What shape are the two ends of a triangular prism? Triangles.

cards.front: Which 3D shape has no vertices and no edges?
cards.back: A sphere.
cards.say: Which 3D shape has no vertices and no edges? A sphere.

cards.back: Sphere, cylinder and cone, because they have curved faces.
cards.say: Which 3D shapes can roll? Sphere, cylinder and cone, because they have curved faces.

cards.front: Which 3D shape is a tin of tomatoes?
cards.back: A cylinder.
cards.say: Which 3D shape is a tin of tomatoes? A cylinder.

cards.front: Which 3D shape is a party hat?
cards.back: A cone.
cards.say: Which 3D shape is a party hat? A cone.

cards.back: A cube.
cards.say: Which 3D shape is a dice? A cube.

cards.back: A sphere.
cards.say: Which 3D shape is a football? A sphere.

cards.front: Which 3D shape has 2 triangle ends and 3 rectangle faces?
cards.back: A triangular prism.
cards.say: Which 3D shape has two triangle ends and three rectangle faces? A triangular prism.

cards.front: Which has more faces: a cube or a square-based pyramid?
cards.back: A cube. 6 faces is more than 5 faces.
cards.say: Which has more faces: a cube or a square-based pyramid? A cube. Six faces is more than five faces.

cards.front: Which has more vertices: a cube or a square-based pyramid?
cards.back: A cube. 8 is more than 5.
cards.say: Which has more vertices: a cube or a square-based pyramid? A cube. Eight is more than five.
